questions.stem: When must a pleasure craft show its navigation lights?
options: Only when crossing a busy shipping lane at night
Only from midnight until the sun comes up
Only when another boat is coming close to you
Sunset to sunrise, and in poor visibility
questions.explanation: Lights are shown from sunset to sunrise, and also in restricted visibility such as fog or heavy rain.

questions.stem: What colour is the port sidelight?
options: Green
White
Yellow
Red
questions.explanation: Port is red and starboard is green.

questions.stem: Over what arc does each sidelight show?
options: 225 degrees forward
135 degrees aft
360 degrees all round
112.5 degrees each
questions.explanation: Each sidelight shows from right ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on its own side, which is 112.5 degrees.

questions.stem: Which light shows white, aft, over an arc of 135 degrees?
options: The masthead light
The stern light
The anchor light
The towing light
questions.explanation: The stern light is white and shows aft over 135 degrees. The masthead light shows forward over 225 degrees.

questions.stem: Which set of lights is correct for a power-driven boat under 12 m underway at night?
options: Sidelights only, with no white light at all
A red all-round light over a green one
All-round white light plus sidelights
A yellow light over a white stern light
questions.explanation: Under 12 m, a power boat may show an all-round white light and sidelights instead of a masthead light and stern light.

questions.stem: A 9 m sailboat is under sail only at night. Which lights may she show?
options: One lantern at the masthead with all three
Sidelights, stern light and masthead light
Only one all-round white light at the top
Two all-round red lights, one over the other
questions.explanation: A sailboat under 20 m may combine her sidelights and stern light in one lantern at the top of the mast. Under sail she shows no masthead light.

questions.stem: A sailboat has her sails up and her engine running. How should she be lit?
options: As a sailing vessel, with sidelights only
As a power boat, with a masthead light
As a vessel at anchor, with one white light
As a vessel not under command, red over red
questions.explanation: A sailboat using her engine is a power-driven vessel, so she shows power-driven lights.

questions.stem: What must a kayaker have ready to show when paddling after sunset?
options: A green light fixed on the bow
A flashing yellow light on the stern
Red and green lights on the hull
A white flashlight or lantern
questions.explanation: A paddle craft must have a white torch or lantern, such as a watertight flashlight, ready to show in time to prevent a collision.

questions.stem: A 6 m boat is anchored overnight in a busy anchorage in Desolation Sound. What light should she show?
options: No light, because she is under 7 m
Red and green sidelights
One all-round white light
A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: The under 7 m exemption does not apply in or near an anchorage or where other boats usually travel.

questions.stem: At night you see a red light, a green light and a white light above them, dead ahead. What is happening?
options: A boat ahead is going away from you
A power boat is heading right at you
A sailboat is crossing ahead from port
A boat is anchored a little way ahead
questions.explanation: Seeing both sidelights and a white light above means a power-driven boat is coming head-on. Both turn to starboard.

questions.stem: You are in a powerboat. You see only a red sidelight and a white light of another powerboat on your starboard bow. What should you do?
options: Hold your course and speed
Turn to port across her bow
Give way; pass astern of her
Speed up to cross ahead of her
questions.explanation: Red on your starboard bow means you see her port side and she has you on her port side. You are the give-way boat.

questions.stem: You see a white light only, and it is getting closer. Which is the most likely situation?
options: You are overtaking her
She is coming head-on
She is crossing from port
She is a tug with a tow
questions.explanation: A white light alone is usually a stern light, so she is ahead and going your way. It can also be a boat at anchor.

questions.stem: A tug shows three white masthead lights in a vertical line. What does this tell you?
options: Her tow is longer than 200 m
She is not under command
She is at anchor with a barge
She is fishing with a net
questions.explanation: A tug towing astern shows two masthead lights, or three if the tow is over 200 m. Never pass between a tug and her tow.

questions.stem: Where is the yellow towing light on a tug towing astern?
options: At the top of the mast
On the bow, near the anchor
Above the stern light
On the barge being towed
questions.explanation: The towing light is yellow and goes in a vertical line above the stern light.
